The investigation into the failing tests [`org.jsoup.select.SelectorTest::handlesCommasInSelector`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/jsoup_21_group_c_arch/src/test/java/org/jsoup/select/SelectorTest.java#L588-L599) and [`org.jsoup.select.SelectorTest::mixCombinatorGroup`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/jsoup_21_group_c_arch/src/test/java/org/jsoup/select/SelectorTest.java#L324-L332) is complete.

### Summary of Investigation
1. **Failing Tests:**
   - In `handlesCommasInSelector`, executing `doc.select("div, li:matches([0-9,]+)")` throws a `java.util.regex.PatternSyntaxException` because commas within pseudo-class expressions (such as regexes) are treated indiscriminately as selector delimiters.
   - In `mixCombinatorGroup`, executing `doc.select(".foo > ol, ol > li + li")` fails the size assertion (`expected:<2> but was:<3>`) when combinators and comma group selectors are combined.
2. **Intended Behavior:**
   - CSS selectors containing commas inside sub-queries or attribute values (e.g. `[name=1,2]`, `:matches([0-9,]+)`) should be preserved and parsed as part of their respective evaluator expressions rather than prematurely splitting the query group.
   - Evaluator grouping and combinators in mixed expressions like `.foo > ol, ol > li + li` should match elements conforming to the selector group specification.

The intended behavior has been specified in Gherkin BDD format in [requirement.feature](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/jsoup_21_group_c_arch/requirement.feature).
